sentences.en: Welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《隐藏大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This week, we're going to tell you the story of a woman who ran an interesting psychological experiment on herself.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们将为您讲述一个女人对自己进行有趣心理学实验的故事。

sentences.en: We look at the science of compassion and why being kind to others can make a big difference to your own life.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨同情心的科学，以及为什么对他人善良会对你自己的生活产生重大影响。

sentences.en: It's easy to say I can't make a difference, but everyone can make a difference.
sentences.zh: 说“我无能为力”很容易，但每个人都能有所作为。

sentences.en: I want to tell you the story about a woman named Kelly Gillespie.
sentences.zh: 我想给你讲一个名叫凯利·吉尔佩的故事。

sentences.en: She's in her early 40s, lives in London, and a couple of years ago, she took a psychology class.
sentences.zh: 她四十岁出头，住在伦敦，几年前她上过一门心理学课。

sentences.en: The class was online, hosted by the education platform Coursera, and it was taught by Scott Plouse.
sentences.zh: 这门课是在线的，由教育平台 Coursera 主办，授课老师是斯科特·普劳斯。

sentences.en: He's a psychologist at Wesleyan University.
sentences.zh: 他是卫斯理大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: And then my life changed after doing Professor Plessis' course, and now I'm studying to be a psychotherapist and counsellor.
sentences.zh: 在上了普莱斯教授的课程后，我的生活改变了，现在我正在学习成为一名心理治疗师和辅导员。

sentences.en: Kelly learned several psychological concepts in the class.
sentences.zh: 凯利在课堂上学到了几个心理学概念。

sentences.en: One is called the norm of reciprocity.
sentences.zh: 其中一个被称为互惠规范。

sentences.en: If you're nice to someone or you open up to them, they're likely to do the same with you.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某人好或者向他们敞开心扉，他们也很可能会对你做同样的事。

sentences.en: She also learned about the power of empathy.
sentences.zh: 她还了解了同理心的力量。

sentences.en: When you put yourself in someone else's shoes, it profoundly changes the relationship that you have with them.
sentences.zh: 当你设身处地为他人着想时，它会深刻地改变你与他们的关系。

sentences.en: Now, lots of people learn about ideas in psychology, but Kelly did something unusual.
sentences.zh: 现在，很多人都在学习心理学理念，但凯利做了一件不寻常的事。

sentences.en: She took what she had learned in the class, and she applied it in her own life.
sentences.zh: 她把在课堂上学到的知识应用到了自己的生活中。

sentences.en: As well, I also write books and novels, so I spend a lot of time at the British Library at King's Cross.
sentences.zh: 另外，我也写书和小说的，所以我花很多时间在国王十字车站的大英图书馆。

sentences.en: My husband works just around the corner from there, so every Friday afternoon I would meet him out of work after I'd been at the British Library researching.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫就在那附近上班，所以每周五下午，我在大英图书馆做完研究后，会去接他下班。

sentences.en: And I would finish about four o'clock, he would finish about six o'clock, so I had a couple of hours to spend.
sentences.zh: 我大约四点钟结束，他大约六点钟结束，所以我有一两个小时的空闲时间。

sentences.en: Sometimes I'd go to the welcome, sometimes I'd just sit and have a coffee and watch people walking by.
sentences.zh: 有时候我会去迎宾处，有时我只是坐着喝杯咖啡，看着行人来来往往。

sentences.en: And it was the same young guy.
sentences.zh: 而且总是那个年轻小伙子。

sentences.en: And always smiling, despite not having anywhere to live or not having a job or any money, but he was always so pleasant.
sentences.zh: 总是面带微笑，尽管无家可居、没有工作也没有钱，但他总是那么亲切。

sentences.en: And it started off simply me giving him what spare change I had.
sentences.zh: 最初只是我把身上的零钱给他。

sentences.en: But it went on for a couple of months, and I got to know him a little bit and know what had happened to make him leave home and come to London.
sentences.zh: 但这持续了几个月，我开始稍微了解他，知道了是什么让他离家出走并来到伦敦。

sentences.en: Kelly learned his name was Simon.
sentences.zh: 凯利得知他的名字叫西蒙。

sentences.en: She asked him if he would sit down with her for a cup of coffee.
sentences.zh: 她问他愿不愿意和她坐下来喝杯咖啡。

sentences.en: He was just walking past on the other side of the road.
sentences.zh: 他当时正走在马路对面的另一边。

sentences.en: I think he walked up and down Tottenham Court Road all day.
sentences.zh: 我想他整天都在托特纳姆法院路走来走去。

sentences.en: And on a night, he would get onto the night buses because he had nowhere to sleep.
sentences.zh: 到了晚上，他会坐夜间巴士，因为他无处可睡。

sentences.en: He would just get on the night bus and travel round and round and round until six o'clock in the morning,
sentences.zh: 他只是上夜班车，一圈又一圈地坐着，直到清晨六点，

sentences.en: hoping to sleep, hoping to not get attacked by the drunks and the people that use the night buses in London.
sentences.zh: 希望能睡一会儿，希望能不被伦敦夜车上的酒鬼和闲杂人员袭击。

sentences.en: To make him feel comfortable, I told him a little bit about my life.
sentences.zh: 为了让他感到自在，我向他透露了一点我的生活。

sentences.en: I told him I was waiting for my husband.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他我在等我丈夫。

sentences.en: I told him how long we'd been together, things like that.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他我们在一起多久了，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And I think by sharing a little bit of my life made him more confident to talk about his life.
sentences.zh: 我想分享我生活中的一点点细节，让他更有信心谈论他的人生。

sentences.en: And I found out, I mean, he wasn't from far away from London, just in Kent on the southeast coaSt.
sentences.zh: 我发现，我的意思是，他离伦敦不远，就在东南海岸的肯特郡。

sentences.en: So only an hour away from London where he grew up.
sentences.zh: 离他长大的伦敦只有一个小时的路程。

sentences.en: And what's going through your head about what you can say or do that would be helpful?
sentences.zh: 你脑子里在想什么可以说或做什么才会有帮助？

sentences.en: He kept mentioning how much he missed his mum, how much he was so close to his mum.
sentences.zh: 他不停地提到他多么想念妈妈，他和他妈妈多么亲近。

sentences.en: And that's a relationship that should never be damaged or taken apart.
sentences.zh: 那是一种永远不应该被破坏或拆散的关系。

sentences.en: So I think that led to me asking him, would he like to speak to his mum?
sentences.zh: 所以我想这促使我问他，他想不想和妈妈通话？

sentences.en: Because my mum died ten years ago.
sentences.zh: 因为我妈妈十年前去世了。

sentences.en: And if someone said to me, now you can speak to your mum, I would bite their hand off.
sentences.zh: 如果有人现在对我说你可以跟你妈妈说话，我会求之不得。

sentences.en: So I just asked him if he wanted to speak to his mum.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是问他想不想跟妈妈说话。

sentences.en: And he said, yeah, he never had a problem with his mum.
sentences.zh: 他说，好啊，他和妈妈之间从来没有问题。

sentences.en: It was because of his father that he left home.
sentences.zh: 是因为他父亲他才离家出走的。

sentences.en: And he loved his mum very much.
sentences.zh: 他非常爱他的妈妈。

sentences.en: And I just thought, if you love someone so much, you shouldn't be so distant from them.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，如果你那么爱一个人，你就不应该离他们这么远。

sentences.en: He has nothing to lose.
sentences.zh: 他没有什么好失去的。

sentences.en: Can you remember your home phone number?
sentences.zh: 你还记得家里的电话号码吗？

sentences.en: Of course, everyone remembers their home phone number.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个人都记得家里的电话号码。

sentences.en: You have nothing to lose.
sentences.zh: 你没什么好失去的。

sentences.en: Because you have nothing.
sentences.zh: 因为你一无所有。

sentences.en: So, let's just give it a go and see what happens.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们试一试，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: He didn't want to at firSt.
sentences.zh: 他一开始并不想。

sentences.en: He didn't want to speak to her.
sentences.zh: 他不想跟她说话。

sentences.en: But eventually, I phoned his mum.
sentences.zh: 但最终，我给他妈妈打了个电话。

sentences.en: And I said, I have a friend of Simon's.
sentences.zh: 我说，我是西蒙的朋友。

sentences.en: And she started crying immediately because she hadn't heard from him in three years.
sentences.zh: 她立刻哭了起来，因为她已经三年没有他的消息了。

sentences.en: She didn't know whether he was alive or dead.
sentences.zh: 她不知道他是死是活。

sentences.en: And immediately, she was so emotional.
sentences.zh: 刹那间，她情绪激动。

sentences.en: And at that moment, I thought, okay, I'm just going to pass the phone over and let them talk.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，我想，好吧，我这就把电话递过去让他们谈谈。

sentences.en: They talked for about 10 minutes, 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 他们谈了大约 10 分钟、15 分钟。

sentences.en: It was quite beautiful to watch because he started off not knowing what to say and being very guarded and defensive.
sentences.zh: 看着这一幕非常美好，因为他开始时不知道该说些什么，而且非常戒备和防备。

sentences.en: And that all broke down within five minutes.
sentences.zh: 这一切在五分钟内就瓦解了。

sentences.en: And he didn't tell them that he was homeless.
sentences.zh: 他没有告诉他们他无家可归。

sentences.en: He didn't mention that at all.
sentences.zh: 他根本没提这件事。

sentences.en: He just said, I've been living in London.
sentences.zh: 他只是说，我一直住在伦敦。

sentences.en: Everything's okay.
sentences.zh: 一切都好。

sentences.en: I'm still alive.
sentences.zh: 我还活着。

sentences.en: He never mentioned his situation at all, though.
sentences.zh: 不过他从未提及自己的处境。

sentences.en: And once the conversation was over, what did you say to him?
sentences.zh: 谈话结束后，你对他说什么了？

sentences.en: And how did things go from there?
sentences.zh: 后来事情进展得怎么样？

sentences.en: I got a little bit bossy, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我变得有点霸道。

sentences.en: And I said, okay, this isn't going to solve itself.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，这不会自己解决的。

sentences.en: So we went to Victoria, coach station.
sentences.zh: 于是我们去了维多利亚长途汽车站。

sentences.en: And I said, if you don't do this, this is the best chance you're going to have of going back home,
sentences.zh: 我说，如果你不这样做，这就是你回家的最好机会，

sentences.en: seeing your mum.
sentences.zh: 去见见你妈妈。

sentences.en: And bought him a ticket on the next bus to go back to South End.
sentences.zh: 并给他买了一张去滨海绍森德的下一班车票。

sentences.en: And that's the last I saw of him.
sentences.zh: 那是最后一次见到他。

sentences.en: He got on the bus and away he went.
sentences.zh: 他上了车，然后就走了。

sentences.en: In terms of what you've done since, Simon, has it changed your behaviour?
sentences.zh: 就你后来所做的事情而言，西蒙，这改变了你的行为吗？

sentences.en: Have you always been somebody who goes up to homeless people and helps them?
sentences.zh: 你一直是个主动接近无家可归者并帮助他们的人吗？

sentences.en: Or have you actually become more proactive?
sentences.zh: 还是说你实际上变得更加积极主动了？

sentences.en: Because you sort of say, I realise that I actually can make a difference.
sentences.zh: 因为你某种程度上说，我意识到我其实可以做出改变。

sentences.en: And maybe I can't make a difference on a mass scale.
sentences.zh: 也许我无法在宏观层面上做出改变。

sentences.en: But I certainly made a difference in one person's life.
sentences.zh: 但我确实改变了一个人的生活。

sentences.en: And that teaches me that I could make a difference in other people's lives, too.
sentences.zh: 这告诉我，我也可以改变其他人的生活。

sentences.en: I think that doing the course with Professor Bluths must definitely open my eyes to the reasons why people don't do something to help.
sentences.zh: 我认为和布鲁斯教授一起上课绝对开阔了我的眼界，让我明白了人们为什么不采取行动去帮助别人。

sentences.en: And I can remember he told us this wonderful story as part of the course, which was told originally, I think, by a Kenyan environmental activist called Wagari Mutamatai.
sentences.zh: 我记得他在课上给我们讲了一个精彩的故事，我想这个故事最初是由一位名叫旺加里·马塔泰的肯尼亚环保主义者讲述的。

sentences.en: And it's a story of a hummingbird in a forest that's being consumed by a wildfire.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于森林里的一只蜂鸟的故事，森林正被野火吞噬。

sentences.en: And all the animals in the forest come out and they're transfixed as they watch the forest burning.
sentences.zh: 森林里所有的动物都跑出来，惊呆地看着森林燃烧。

sentences.en: And they feel very overwhelmed and very powerless, except this one little hummingbird that says, I'm going to do something about this fire.
sentences.zh: 他们感到非常无所适从、无能为力，除了这只小蜂鸟，它说我要对这场火做点什么。

sentences.en: And Professor Bluths told us this story about all the animals laughing at this little hummingbird as it flew backwards and forwards from the nearer stream.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯教授给我们讲了这个故事，说当这只小蜂鸟在附近的溪流来回飞翔时，所有的动物都在嘲笑它。

sentences.en: Coming up next, the person whom Kelly says changed her life, her teacher, psychologist Scott Plouse of Wesleyan University.
sentences.zh: 接下来，凯利说改变了她一生的人，她的老师，卫斯理大学的心理学家斯科特·普劳斯。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I first met Scott many years ago.
sentences.zh: 我很多年前就认识斯科特了。

sentences.en: He's a very smart guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个非常聪明的人。

sentences.en: But the thing that leaps out when you meet him is that he's a really nice guy.
sentences.zh: 但当你见到他时，最显眼的特点是他真的是个很好的人。

sentences.en: Actually, scratch that.
sentences.zh: 其实，收回这句话。

sentences.en: Nice doesn't cut it.
sentences.zh: 光说人好还不够。

sentences.en: Scott radiates kindness.
sentences.zh: 斯科特散发着善良。

sentences.en: The class where Scott connected with Kelly was an online class.
sentences.zh: 斯科特与凯利结缘的课堂是一门在线课程。

sentences.en: Believe it or not, more than 250,000 students from around the world signed up for the class.
sentences.zh: 信不信由你，来自世界各地的 25 万多名学生报名了这门课程。

sentences.en: And at the end of it, Scott gave Kelly and his other students an assignment.
sentences.zh: 在课程结束时，斯科特给凯利和他的其他学生布置了一项作业。

sentences.en: It was called the Day of Compassion.
sentences.zh: 它被称为同情心之日。

sentences.en: Students had to spend one day being deliberately kind and generous toward others.
sentences.zh: 学生们必须花一天时间对他人刻意表现出善良和慷慨。

sentences.en: Scott asked them to notice how these actions changed the way they felt about themselves.
sentences.zh: 斯科特要求他们注意这些行为如何改变了他们对自己的看法。

sentences.en: I asked Scott to tell me what students find when they do this.
sentences.zh: 我请斯科特告诉我，学生在做这件事时发现了什么。

sentences.en: Students often report that it's transformative, that they're really surprised at the reaction,
sentences.zh: 学生们经常反应这是具有变革意义的，他们对这种反应感到非常惊讶，

sentences.en: that people are so overwhelmingly positive that it starts to feed on itself.
sentences.zh: 人们的反应是如此压倒性的积极，以至于它开始形成良性循环。

sentences.en: And by the end of the day, they report that this is a different side of me that I didn't recognize was there.
sentences.zh: 到了一天结束时，他们报告说这是我未曾认出的自己身上不同的一面。

sentences.en: And is that because they are behaving differently or other people are behaving differently?
sentences.zh: 这是因为他们的行为不同还是其他人表现不同？

sentences.en: What's the cause?
sentences.zh: 原因是什么？

sentences.en: What's driving this change?
sentences.zh: 是什么在推动这种变化？

sentences.en: Oftentimes, it seems that compassion is contagious.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，同情心似乎具有传染性。

sentences.en: We've talked about paying it forward, the idea that if you do something good for another person,
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过爱的传递，也就是如果你对另一个人做好事，

sentences.en: that that gives the other person a kind of lift.
sentences.zh: 这会给对方带来一种振奋。

sentences.en: And then that person, in turn, will do something for somebody else.
sentences.zh: 然后这个人反过来会为其他人做点什么。

sentences.en: And it sets off a kind of chain reaction.
sentences.zh: 这就引发了一种连锁反应。

sentences.en: So it's not just find the one dramatic thing that you can do in the day that can change the life of someone else.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是在一天中找到你可以做的能改变别人生活的一件轰动的事。

sentences.en: You're actually asking people to change the way they live that day.
sentences.zh: 你实际上是在要求人们改变他们那一天的生活方式。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, Martin Luther King Jr.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，小马丁·路德·金

sentences.en: had a wonderful quote as well about the effect that you have just in eating breakfast,
sentences.zh: 也有一句精彩的名言，关于你仅仅吃早餐所产生的影响，

sentences.en: the number of lives that you touch, where the cereal comes from, where the packaging comes from,
sentences.zh: 你接触到的生活数量，麦片从哪里来，包装从哪里来，

sentences.en: who brought the cereal to you, where did the milk come from, and so on.
sentences.zh: 谁把麦片带给你的，牛奶从哪里来，等等。

sentences.en: And before you know it, you've touched thousands of lives without even realizing it.
sentences.zh: 不知不觉中，你在甚至没有意识到的时候已经触动了成千上万人的生活。

sentences.en: So the students are asked to look deeply, to think deeply about their life choices, their behaviors,
sentences.zh: 因此，学生们被要求深入观察，深入思考他们的生活选择、他们的行为，

sentences.en: and to think about it specifically in terms of compassion.
sentences.zh: 并专门从同情心的角度来思考它。

sentences.en: So when you're eating your cereal, even if you know that these thousands of people have touched your cereal,
sentences.zh: 所以当你吃麦片的时候，即使你知道这成千上万的人接触过你的麦片，

sentences.en: how do you act compassionately toward all of them?
sentences.zh: 你如何对他们所有人表现出同情心？

sentences.en: Well, in some cases, you might be thinking about people who are working under unfair labor conditions.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在某些情况下，你可能会想到在不公平劳动条件下工作的人。

sentences.en: You might be thinking, if I throw away this food, what else am I throwing away?
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，如果我扔掉这些食物，我还扔掉了什么？

sentences.en: You might think about when you drive to work, could you be bicycling?
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，当你开车上班时，你能骑自行车吗？

sentences.en: Could you be walking?
sentences.zh: 你能步行吗？

sentences.en: What consequences are there for other people?
sentences.zh: 对其他人有什么后果？

sentences.en: So there are many, many different connections that we normally don't have time to think about.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多很多我们平时没有时间思考的不同联系。

sentences.en: And in this assignment, I ask students to simply slow down and think about those connections.
sentences.zh: 在这个作业中，我要求学生们放慢脚步，思考这些联系。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting, when we actually start thinking about this in great detail,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，当我们真正开始详细思考这一点时，

sentences.en: we often realize then that we're making choices that, even though we think of ourselves as being good people,
sentences.zh: 我们经常会意识到，我们正在做出这样的选择：尽管我们认为自己是好人，

sentences.en: those choices are often unsupportable by the values that we claim to have.
sentences.zh: 但这些选择往往无法支撑我们声称拥有的价值观。

sentences.en: You know, in my book, I talk about the idea that, you know, I was discussing the role that childhood vaccines play
sentences.zh: 你知道，在我的书里，我谈到了这样一个观点，我当时在讨论儿童疫苗所起的作用

sentences.en: in saving children's lives in many parts of the world, and how, you know, for $200,
sentences.zh: 在世界许多地方拯救儿童的生命，以及，你知道的，只需 200 美元，

sentences.en: you could probably save a child's life in a poor country by making sure that she has access to just
sentences.zh: 你就可以在贫穷国家通过确保她获得一套儿童疫苗来拯救一个孩子的生命。

sentences.en: a suite of childhood vaccines.
sentences.zh: 这套疫苗只需

sentences.en: And when I gave my daughter a birthday party, this was a couple years ago,
sentences.zh: 而当我给女儿办生日派对时，这是几年前的事了，

sentences.en: and the birthday party cost $200 or $250, I had a moment where I stopped and said,
sentences.zh: 生日派对花了两百或二百五十美元，我当时突然停下来，对自己说：

sentences.en: I'm spending $250 on my child's birthday party, and the same $250 could save the life of a child
sentences.zh: 我花二百五十美元给我孩子办生日派对，而同样的二百五十美元却能拯救

sentences.en: halfway around the world.
sentences.zh: 远在世界另一端的一个孩子的生命。

sentences.en: Now, how is it possible that one child's birthday party could be more important than another child's life?
sentences.zh: 那么，一个孩子的生日派对怎么可能比另一个孩子的生命更重要呢？

sentences.en: And I felt like a terrible human being.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己是个糟糕透顶的人。

sentences.en: Well, I'm sorry you feel terrible about that, but at least having a level of awareness, I think,
sentences.zh: 嗯，很遗憾你会有这种糟糕的感觉，但我觉得，至少有这种觉悟

sentences.en: can be a positive thing.
sentences.zh: 可以是一件积极的事。

sentences.en: The Princeton philosopher Peter Singer has a great example of this.
sentences.zh: 普林斯顿大学的哲学家彼得·辛格有一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: He talks about somebody who's walking past some water and sees a child drowning,
sentences.zh: 他讲到有人走过一片水域，看到一个孩子在溺水，

sentences.en: and this person happens to be in very fancy clothes, let's say an Armani suit or some very expensive shoes.
sentences.zh: 这个人正好穿着非常华丽的衣服，比方说阿玛尼西装或非常昂贵的鞋子。

sentences.en: And the question is, if you're the only one there and the only one capable of saving the child,
sentences.zh: 问题是，如果你是那里唯一的人，也是唯一有能力拯救这个孩子的人，

sentences.en: and there's no time to spare, should you, in fact, ruin your suit?
sentences.zh: 而且时间紧迫，你真的应该毁掉你的西装吗？

sentences.en: Should you ruin your shoes and save the life?
sentences.zh: 你应该毁掉你的鞋子去救人性命吗？

sentences.en: Let's say that you would lose $200 doing that.
sentences.zh: 假设你这么做会损失二百美元。

sentences.en: And almost everybody would say, of course, the child's life is worth more than the $200.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有人都会说，当然，孩子的生命比二百美元更有价值。

sentences.en: And then Peter Singer turns around and says, well, what if we could demonstrate that there's a child's life
sentences.zh: 然后彼得·辛格话锋一转说，如果我们能证明，在地球的另一端

sentences.en: halfway around the world and that $200 would be sufficient to save that life?
sentences.zh: 有一个孩子的生命，而二百美元就足以挽救那个生命呢？

sentences.en: Why aren't you spending the $200?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不花这二百美元？

sentences.en: And of course, the question is, lots of us don't.
sentences.zh: 当然，问题在于，我们很多人都没有这么做。

sentences.en: The child in the pond who's drowning feels visceral to us and feels like our responsibility
sentences.zh: 水池里溺水的孩子让我们感到真切，觉得那是我们的责任，

sentences.en: in ways that the child halfway around the world does not feel like our responsibility.
sentences.zh: 而远在世界另一端的孩子却不会让我们有这种责任感。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: There's an immediacy there.
sentences.zh: 这里有一种紧迫感。

sentences.en: There's a vividness and there's different consequences when you see somebody personally
sentences.zh: 当你亲眼看到某人需要帮助，而不是把对方当作抽象遥远的存在时，

sentences.en: in need, rather than having somebody be abstract and remote.
sentences.zh: 会有生动的感受，也会产生不同的结果。

sentences.en: And people will say to themselves, well, maybe that's true, but there are so many children
sentences.zh: 人们会对自己说，好吧，也许这是真的，但有那么多的儿童

sentences.en: in need.
sentences.zh: 需要帮助。

sentences.en: If I gave each one $200, I would be left in poverty.
sentences.zh: 如果我给每个人二百美元，我就会变得一贫如洗。

sentences.en: I can't possibly do that.
sentences.zh: 我根本做不到这一点。

sentences.en: And this is where psychology comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是心理学发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: We tell ourselves stories about why it's okay not to help, why it's okay not to help once.
sentences.zh: 我们会给自己编造各种理由，解释为什么不帮忙是可以的，为什么偶尔不帮忙是可以的。

sentences.en: And we say, well, because if I then did once, I would have to do a hundred, and I couldn't
sentences.zh: 我们会说，因为如果我帮了一次，我就得帮一百次，我根本

sentences.en: possibly do that.
sentences.zh: 做不到这一点。

sentences.en: But in fact, sometimes you can do one, and one is better than zero.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，有时候你可以帮一次，而帮一次总比一次都不帮强。

sentences.en: That's social psychologist Scott Plouse from Wesleyan University.
sentences.zh: 这是卫斯理安大学的社会心理学家斯科特·普劳斯。

sentences.en: When we return, we'll hear a poem from the writer Karen Enns, and we're going to issue
sentences.zh: 稍后，我们将聆听作家凯伦·恩斯的一首诗，我们还将发起

sentences.en: a challenge of our own.
sentences.zh: 我们自己的挑战。

sentences.en: I want to leave you today with a poem.
sentences.zh: 今天我想留下一首诗送给大家。

sentences.en: It's by Canadian poet Karen Enns, from her book, Ordinary Hours.
sentences.zh: 它出自加拿大诗人凯伦·恩斯的诗集《平常的时辰》。

sentences.en: Karen came to write this poem after a moment when she experienced the power of compassion,
sentences.zh: 凯伦写这首诗是在她经历了一次感受到同情力量的时刻之后，

sentences.en: a small gesture from a stranger that lifted her heart.
sentences.zh: 那是陌生人一个小小的举动，却温暖了她的心。

sentences.en: We asked her to read the poem and tell us about that moment.
sentences.zh: 我们请她朗读这首诗，并给我们讲讲那个时刻。

sentences.en: A gull will almost land.
sentences.zh: 一只海鸥几乎要降落。

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 继续走。

sentences.en: Everything is good.
sentences.zh: 一切都很好。

sentences.en: Up ahead, a gull will almost land in front of you.
sentences.zh: 前方，一只海鸥几乎要降落在你面前。

sentences.en: Its wings will catch the current on a knife edge.
sentences.zh: 它的双翼在刀刃般的气流中支撑。

sentences.en: Its flimsy element of bone will keep it motionless above the ground for just so long.
sentences.zh: 它那脆弱的骨骼元素将使它在地面上方悬停片刻。

sentences.en: And that pure pose will meet the light as if a god had ordered it to catch your eye.
sentences.zh: 那种纯粹的姿态迎着光芒，仿佛神明命令它去吸引你的目光。

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 继续走。

sentences.en: We are all defined by something like surrender.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都被某种类似于臣服的东西所定义。

sentences.en: Not a giving in exactly.
sentences.zh: 并非完全是妥协。

sentences.en: Not a yielding.
sentences.zh: 也并非屈服。

sentences.en: But suspension.
sentences.zh: 而是悬停。

sentences.en: Perfect justice as the holding becomes opening.
sentences.zh: 当这种支撑化为敞开时，便是完美的正义。

sentences.en: As the moment of arrival on dry ground, small and blazing with intent, becomes departure.
sentences.zh: 当抵达干燥陆地的时刻——渺小而燃烧着意图——化为离去时。

sentences.en: I think that most of us, at some point in our lives,
sentences.zh: 我想我们大多数人在生活中的某个时刻，

sentences.en: in dark times maybe, are looking for some kind of message from something, someone, someplace.
sentences.zh: 也许是在黑暗的时期，都在寻找来自某物、某人、某地的某种信息。

sentences.en: And that's where the starting point of this poem comes about.
sentences.zh: 这正是这首诗的起点由来。

sentences.en: I was walking down the street a few years ago and a bus stopped at the stoplight and there was an elderly man who looked out the window at me and he nodded.
sentences.zh: 几年前我走在街上，一辆公交车在红绿灯前停下，有个老人在窗户看着我，他对我点了点头。

sentences.en: And in that nod, in that gesture, there was a kind of urging on.
sentences.zh: 而在那个点头中，在那个手势中，有一种鼓励的意味。

sentences.en: And I kept that image with me and I think that's what drove the beginning of the poem, at least anyway, was his very kind look toward me.
sentences.zh: 我把那个画面留在了记忆里，我想这就是推动这首诗开篇的力量，至少，是他对我那非常慈祥的眼神。

sentences.en: And I took that as a message.
sentences.zh: 我把这当作一个讯息。

sentences.en: That was Karen Enns talking about her poem, A Gull Will Almost Land, from the collection, Ordinary Hours.
sentences.zh: 以上是凯伦·恩斯谈论她收录于诗集《平常的时辰》中的诗作《一只海鸥几乎要降落》。

sentences.en: What would you do if you had to spend one day beaming compassion into the world?
sentences.zh: 如果你必须花一天时间向世界播撒同情，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: It could be something small, acknowledging a stranger.
sentences.zh: 它可以是一件小事，向陌生人致意。

sentences.en: It could be something big, changing the direction of another person's life.
sentences.zh: 它可以是一件大事，改变另一个人的人生方向。

sentences.en: Please try it and tell us what you found.
sentences.zh: 请尝试一下，并告诉我们你的发现。

sentences.en: We'll put some of the stories you share with us on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们会把你们分享的一些故事放到播客节目中。

sentences.en: You can find us on Facebook at Hidden Brain or send us an email at hiddenbrain at npr.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在脸书上搜索 Hidden Brain 找到我们，或者发邮件至 hiddenbrain@npr.org。

sentences.en: This episode of the Hidden Brain podcast was produced by Cara McGurk-Allison and Maggie Penman.
sentences.zh: 本期 Hidden Brain 播客由卡拉·麦格克-艾利森和玛吉·彭曼制作。

sentences.en: Special help from Jenna Weiss-Berman, Megan Cain, and Rachel Ward.
sentences.zh: 詹娜·韦斯-伯曼、梅根·凯恩和雷切尔·沃德提供了特别协助。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆，这里是美国国家公共电台。
